preamble: The reduction of a voiceless postalveolar affricate /tʃ/ to a voiceless postalveolar fricative [ʃ] is an example of deaffrication. This process involves the loss of the initial stop component of the affricate, leaving only the fricative portion.

examples.note: Word-initially Erzya has the affricate where Moksha has the fricative.

sources: Ladefoged, P., & Maddieson, I. (1996). The Sounds of the World's Languages. Blackwell. https://www.wiley.com/en-us/The+Sounds+of+the+World%27s+Languages-p-9780631198154
Campbell, L. (2013). Historical Linguistics: An Introduction (3rd ed.). Edinburgh University Press; MIT Press. https://lccn.loc.gov/2012038044
